correctness.rationale: The odd-indexed set O_i is a skew fort in each even cycle, giving disjoint one-token-per-block lower bound k. For a candidate selecting one odd vertex from every cycle, deleting the selected set leaves a forest (indeed a connected tree) with two even-size arms at every port. In any perfect matching, each port must match a bridge; hence residual perfect matchings correspond exactly to perfect matchings of T. For forests, empty-set skew forcing iff perfect matching follows from a directed permutation of all force vertices and leaf-edge induction. Thus Z^- equals k iff T has a perfect matching, and all minima are coordinate choices O_i. Cartesian clique product exchange, edge count N sum_i(r_i-1)/2, diameter k, and all-isolated sliding follow immediately. Independently enumerated all size-2 successful sets in connected C4/C4, C4/C6, C6/C6 bridge sources and obtained 4,6,9 exactly; all are distinct odd pairs, not an all-T finite proof.
